points.description: Focal length in pixels: fx = f / pixel size = 16 mm / 0.005 mm = 3200 pixels (fy = fx as pixels are square). Full marks need the correct value 3200 px.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark for the correct method with a slip in the value; 0 if the formula is wrong (e.g. multiplying f by pixel size).

levels.says: Uses the correct relation fx = f / pixel width (or 16 mm / 5 µm) but makes a unit-conversion or arithmetic slip, so the value is not 3200.

points.description: Field of view width on the belt = 160 mm. Sensor width 1280 × 5 µm = 6.4 mm, times 400/16 = 25 (or 1280 × Z/fx). Any valid route to 160 mm earns the mark.

Distance on the belt per pixel = 160 mm / 1280 = 0.125 mm per pixel (equivalently Z/fx = 400/3200). Accept 0.125 mm/pixel or 125 µm/pixel. A value consistent with the student's own wrong FOV does not earn this mark unless it equals 0.125 mm.

rubric.notes: Full marks: fx = 3200 px (2), FOV = 160 mm (1), 0.125 mm per pixel (1). Either route (sensor size × do/f, or Z/fx) is acceptable. One mark is given for fx if the method is right but the arithmetic is wrong; otherwise no part marks.
rubric.answer_key:
(i) fx = f / pixel width = 16 mm / 0.005 mm = 3200 pixels (fy = fx).
(ii) Sensor width = 1280 × 5 µm = 6.4 mm. FOV = 6.4 × 400/16 = 160 mm. One pixel = 160/1280 = 0.125 mm (check: Z/fx = 400/3200 = 0.125 mm). Final answer: 0.125 mm per pixel (FOV 160 mm, fx = 3200 px).
